mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages indicates a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both exceed 6-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages in a post-recession recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE and rising PAYEMS) above its pre-pandemic trend signals improved labor supply, which increases productive capacity and supports higher corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS jointly indicate LFPR above pre-pandemic trend
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when labor force participation recovers above its pre-pandemic trend.

mechanism_narrative: Real personal savings (RSAFS) falling below its 5-year average while consumer spending (GDPC1) remains flat indicates a shift from saving to spending, which boosts near-term consumption demand and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS falls below its 5-year average and GDPC1 is flat.
